title: Data Types
summary: The kinds of values Luau can store: nil, boolean, number, string, table, function, thread, plus Roblox types like Instance, Vector3, CFrame, and Enum.

details.heading: Roblox adds many more
details.body: `typeof()` also recognizes engine types: `"Instance"`, `"Vector3"`, `"Vector2"`, `"CFrame"`, `"Color3"`, `"UDim2"`, `"Enum"`, `"EnumItem"`, `"TweenInfo"`, `"RaycastResult"`, `"DateTime"`, and more. The plain Lua `type()` function reports most of these as `"userdata"` — prefer `typeof()`.

details.heading: Numbers
details.body: Luau numbers are double-precision floats by default. Integer division `//` and bitwise operators exist, but there is no separate integer runtime type in the default mode.

explanation.whatItIs: Every value in Luau has a type that determines what you can do with it: you can add numbers, concatenate strings, index tables, call functions. Unlike many languages, variables don't have types — *values* do, and a variable can hold any type at any time.
explanation.whyItExists: Types define behavior. `"5" + 5` is an error while `5 + 5` is 10; knowing types tells you which operations are legal and which will error.
whenToUse: Use `typeof(value)` to check what you're dealing with before operating on it
Use type checking annotations (`local x: number = 5`) to catch type bugs before running
whenNotToUse: Don't over-check types defensively — if your code controls the value, trust it. Check at boundaries (remote arguments, user input) instead
explanation.mentalModel:
| Type      | Example                          | typeof() says |
|-----------|----------------------------------|---------------|
| nil       | `nil`                            | "nil"         |
| boolean   | `true`, `false`                  | "boolean"     |
| number    | `42`, `3.5`                      | "number"      |
| string    | `"hello"`                        | "string"      |
| table     | `{}`, `{1,2}`, `{coins = 5}`     | "table"       |
| function  | `print`, `function() end`        | "function"    |
| thread    | `coroutine.create(f)`            | "thread"      |
| Roblox    | `Instance.new("Part")`           | "Instance"    |
tips: `typeof(x)` is Roblox-friendly; `type(x)` is the classic Lua version — both exist, but `typeof` gives nicer answers for engine values
`nil` is the type of 'no value'. A variable that is nil effectively doesn't hold anything
Tables are the one container type — arrays, dictionaries, objects, and modules are all tables
commonMistakes: Doing math on strings: `"10" + 5` happens to work (auto-coercion) but `"10 apples" + 5` errors — convert with `tonumber()` first
Expecting `type(game.Workspace)` to say "Workspace" — it says "userdata"; use `typeof()` or `:IsA()` for Instances

examples.title: Inspecting types with typeof()
examples.code:
print(typeof(nil))                    --> nil
print(typeof(true))                   --> boolean
print(typeof(42))                     --> number
print(typeof("hi"))                   --> string
print(typeof({}))                     --> table
print(typeof(print))                  --> function
print(typeof(workspace) )             --> Instance
print(typeof(Vector3.new(0,0,0)))     --> Vector3
print(typeof(Enum.HumanoidRig))       --> Enum
examples.whyItWorks: `typeof()` returns a string naming the value's type, including Roblox engine types.

examples.title: Guarding with a type check
examples.code:
local function double(value)
    if typeof(value) ~= "number" then
        warn("double() expected a number, got " .. typeof(value))
        return nil
    end
    return value * 2
end

print(double(21))     --> 42
print(double("hi"))   --> nil (with a warning)
